_comment: Reference expectations for the semantic-comparison layer (clinical pathology). These assert BEHAVIOUR of the comparator, independent of any fingerprint. Fingerprints may accelerate these checks but must never be their authority (INV-7).

comparisons.note: Exactly one clinical field corrected. hba1c and interpretation must NOT appear as clinical changes despite Catalog V2's relabel/range change, because the amendment inherited V1 snapshots (INV-10). issue_number/issue_date differ by design (Option A) and are provenance metadata, NOT a clinical diff -- the CLINICAL comparator must ignore them.

comparisons.left: R100/V1 rendered while Catalog V1 is current
comparisons.right: R100/V1 rendered while Catalog V2 is current
comparisons.note: Same finalized version viewed under two catalog states. Snapshot rendering means both show 'Fasting Blood Sugar (70-100)'. If either side ever shows 'Fasting Plasma Glucose' or range 74-106, that is an INV-2 violation, not a legitimate difference.

comparisons.left: R100/V1 rendered by renderer r1 (font A, pagination X)
comparisons.right: R100/V1 rendered by renderer r2 (font B, pagination Y)
comparisons.note: Different bytes, different line wrapping. Per R6 (semantic + structural equivalence), semantic comparison must report clinically EQUAL (INV-6). A PDF binary diff is NOT an acceptable comparator.

comparisons.left: a report using interpretation.glucose=glu_prediabetes, issued under V1
comparisons.right: the same report retrieved after V2 deprecated that option
comparisons.note: Deprecation in V2 must not alter or break the historical report (INV-8). It still renders 'Pre-diabetes' from its snapshot; no silent remap.
